architecture.mechanism: Decentralized energy delivery integration with centralized grid assets to optimize system resilience and efficiency under high demand variability
architecture.intervention: Implement a hybrid thermal management system combining immersion cooling with a decentralized, adaptive fluid circulation network that dynamically redistributes thermal load across racks during high-power density (>70 kW/rack) conditions, leveraging localized heat sinks and a centralized heat exchange loop to prevent dielectric breakdown and maintain inlet temperatures within ASHRAE limits
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced fluid breakdown risk, stabilized dielectric performance, and sustained PUE <1.05 by mitigating convection degradation through decentralized thermal load balancing and centralized heat recovery
architecture.falsification_test: Monitor fluid dielectric strength and inlet temperature stability across 10 racks under stepped power density loads (70–120 kW/rack) for 72 hours; compare against baseline immersion cooling failure rate and PUE metrics
